top_categories.workout_context: 75ft/mi signals a climbing-heavy course. Sustained sub-threshold and threshold work builds the steady power needed without turning the opening climb into the day’s hardest effort.

Road-specific control matters at Tour de Mátra Gran Fondo. Practice on mountain passes: use smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 100 miles.
Race-pace efforts that mimic Tour de Mátra Gran Fondo's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before July.
At Tour de Mátra Gran Fondo, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.
At mile 60 of 100, glycogen is gone. This workout teaches your body to produce watts on fumes.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Tour de Mátra Gran Fondo. Train it until it feels boring.
7,567ft of climbing makes aerobic ceiling relevant when the grade or pace changes. VO2max work supports those hard moments; sustained climbing and conservative pacing remain the spine.
7,567ft of climbing on grades that change every minute. You need to switch from seated to standing without losing rhythm.
Brief efforts above sustainable power can come from grade changes, positioning, or closing a gap at Tour de Mátra Gran Fondo. Train them without letting those efforts derail the longer pacing plan.
Every hard session works better with a bigger aerobic base. At 100 miles, base fitness is the difference between racing and surviving.
Endurance with intensity spikes baked in. Exactly what 7,567ft of climbing on mountain passes does to your power file on race day.
Steeper ramps, positioning, or pace changes on mountain passes can demand short hard efforts. Practice them without compromising the sustained work that defines the course.

race_overlay.weather: July in Gyöngyös, Hungary — Mátra climatic health resort (clean therapeutic air); late May mild 15-25°C days, possible mountain showers[1][2][3]. Rehearse adaptable layers and race-day kit changes in the final 2 weeks before Tour de Mátra Gran Fondo. Use the organizer's current forecast and safety instructions for final choices.
race_overlay.nutrition: Target 60–80g carbs/hour for Tour de Mátra Gran Fondo’s 100 miles. Start fueling within the first 30 minutes — early fueling prevents late-race collapse. Bonking at mile 60 is a nutrition failure, not a fitness failure.
race_overlay.altitude: Altitude may change sustainable power and recovery at Tour de Mátra Gran Fondo. Use conservative pacing and test any travel strategy before the event.
race_overlay.terrain: The course profile at Tour de Mátra Gran Fondo rewards specific practice. Include regular rides on mountain passes to build confidence.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on TT Threshold, Road Specific, and Race Simulation to prepare you for 100 miles of mountain passes in Gyöngyös, Hungary.
